questions.question: Select the best summary of the Australian Consumer Law (ACL) and how it relates to customer service.
options: The ACL provides comprehensive rights and safeguards for consumers when dealing with businesses in relation to a range of matters, including consumer rights and guarantees, warranties and refunds, complaints and misleading or deceptive conduct.
The ACL provides comprehensive rights and safeguards for consumers of food, alcohol and tobacco products only; it has little bearing on the provision of customer service in other settings.
The ACL primarily focuses on supermarket products, such as incorrect scanning and false advertising, and as such, it has minimal impact in other customer service contexts.
answer_texts: The ACL provides comprehensive rights and safeguards for consumers when dealing with businesses in relation to a range of matters, including consumer rights and guarantees, warranties and refunds, complaints and misleading or deceptive conduct.

questions.question: Select the best summary of Public Health Acts and how they relate to customer service.
options: Public Health Acts primarily focus on regulations and measures related to public health, safety, and hygiene; they have no relevance to customer service contexts.

Public Health Acts are a collection of laws designed to ensure the provision of exceptional customer service across various industries, emphasising the importance of customer satisfaction and quality assurance.

Public Health Acts primarily focus on regulations and measures related to public health, safety, and hygiene. They may relate to customer service in regard to matters such as the safety and security of staff and customers, mental health support and emergency response protocols.
answer_texts: Public Health Acts primarily focus on regulations and measures related to public health, safety, and hygiene. They may relate to customer service in regard to matters such as the safety and security of staff and customers, mental health support and emergency response protocols.

questions.question: The Privacy Act 1988 (Cth.) promotes the sharing of customer information without consent, reducing the need for repetition and facilitating better customer service.
options: The Privacy Act 1988 (Cth.) has a significant effect on how businesses manage and protect customer information, for example, the protection of personal information, data breach notifications, and consent around the collection and use of customer data, which in turn can influence the customer service experience.
The Privacy Act 1988 (Cth.) mainly focuses on protecting customer service representatives' privacy and has little impact on customer data protection.

questions.question: Q5. What are four (4) typical examples of organisational policies and procedures that relate to the management of handling disrespectful, aggressive or abusive customers?
options: Conflict resolution competitions and contest
Incident reporting and record keeping
Using humour to defuse aggressive customer interactions
Incident response methods
Customer aggressor rewards
Complaint handling and resolution
Escalation protocol
Q6.  Select four (4) ways organisational policies and procedures help support a positive and safe environment for staff when dealing with disrespectful, aggressive or abusive customers.

questions.question: Setting clear expectations for staff behaviour and customer interactions
options: Establishing health and safety protocols
Providing techniques for customer provocation
Providing de-escalation techniques
Providing debriefing procedures
Establishing guidelines around the ‘customer is always right’ principle, even when   rude or aggressive

options: Problems with cost and pricing
Social media trends
Service or product delays
Holiday periods, such as Christmas
Individual character traits and attributes
Misunderstandings of staff instructions
Exceeded customer expectations
Refusal or ejection from premises

questions.question: Staff uniforms

Unavailability of stock
Aesthetics (décor) of the premises
Store location

questions.question: Select two (2) reasons it is important for customer service staff to develop an awareness of the signs of potential customer disruption.
options: To psychologically profile customers and create a blacklist of troublesome ones
To time breaks so as to avoid possible difficult interactions
To proactively manage and de-escalate situations before they worsen
To pre-empt customer frustrations and take appropriate measures to address concerns and provide solutions
answer_texts: To proactively manage and de-escalate situations before they worsen
To pre-empt customer frustrations and take appropriate measures to address concerns and provide solutions

questions.question: What are five (5) examples of disrespectful, aggressive or abusive customer behaviour?
options: Unwillingness or inability to calm down
Request to speak to a supervisor
Use of inappropriate language, including racial slurs
Inability to effectively communicate in local language
Refusal to follow staff instructions
Expression of dissatisfaction about excessive wait times
Verbal or physical aggression
Requests for information about products or services
Hostile group behaviour
answer_texts: Unwillingness or inability to calm down
Use of inappropriate language, including racial slurs

questions.question: High employee retention
options: Improved customer satisfaction
High staff turnover
Increased productivity
Low staff morale and high job dissatisfaction
Increased sick leave absences
Maintained staff welfare and wellbeing
answer_texts: Low staff morale and high job dissatisfaction

questions.question: With regard to disrespectful, aggressive or abusive customer behaviour, select three (3) ways associated risks to the business can be mitigated?
options: Downplaying the impact of such behaviour on staff and the business
Providing staff training and skill development
Having clear and established policies and procedures
Removing accountability from customers for their behaviour
Offering professional support services for staff
Disregarding incident reporting and documentation
answer_texts: Providing staff training and skill development
Having clear and established policies and procedures
Offering professional support services for staff
